title: Is ‘Vintage Violence’ the Future of Movies? Inside the Frantic Chase Movie Built for Phone-Addicted Audiences: It’s a ‘New Approach to Viewing’
description:
Eugene Kotlyarenko’s “Vintage Violence” is a movie that speaks directly to America’s phone-obsessed culture.

	The kinetic action adventure, which h
body:
Eugene Kotlyarenko’s “Vintage Violence” is a movie that speaks directly to America’s phone-obsessed culture.

	The kinetic action adventure, which has its world premiere Sept. 12 at Toronto International Film Festival, is about livestreamer Carter Tipe (Cole Sprouse) who stumbles upon a supply of vintage denim in a cave. He’s encouraged by a Japanese fan named Izumi (Kiko Mizuhara) to bring it to her country in order to sell it for a small fortune. Once there, things get frantic quickly as Carter is on the run from the police, criminals, hustlers and the Yakuza.
	

	But “Vintage Violence” feels so modern thanks to its kaleidoscopic visuals. The screen is sometimes bifurcated between Carter’s livestream, which itself gets clogged with fan comments and emojis, and people watching it in Japan. The camera moves constantly and visual information — lights, split screens, colors, sounds, movement — floods the viewer. It feels like a film working to speak to an audience that grew up with second-screen culture, used to scanning their phones as they’re watching a film or show.


	Kotlyarenko, whose previous film was the similarly internet-minded 2020 thriller “Spree,” says the online style was essential for the story he wanted to tell.

	“My thesis at that point is that we’re so connected and deeply involved with screens that it rewires our brains to process information differently, to process storytelling differently,” he says. “Over the last two decades, I’ve seen how it’s changed not just our attention, but our expectation for what storytelling is and our participation. The lure of social media and video games, it’s active immersion rather than passive like cinema. So I thought it’s very important, grammatically, because these screens are so dominant, to figure out ways to aesthetically integrate them into cinema language, but also grapple with this new approach to viewing, which is so scattered, schizophrenic and all over the place. The challenge and the joy is figuring out how to guide and direct people on where to look, how to look, when to look.”
	

	Even though Kotlyarenko’s technique is extremely modern, he is comforted by knowing that some of cinema’s greats are also into pushing visual and tech boundaries.

	“One of the great adventures and joys of trying to innovate something is using those cinematic techniques and finding inspiration in other filmmakers,” he says. “There are filmmakers who seem very technologically in tune, like Brian De Palma, or Pedro Almodóvar is always doing something that feels very contemporary technologically. So I’m looking to what’s cool about how the masters think about stuff and then trying to put my own energy and spin on it.”

	Another important visual element came from nodding to Japanese film culture, as so much of the movie was shot there with a local crew. Kotlyarenko, along with his DP Sean Price Williams, was able to experiment in the footsteps of Japanese cinema legends.

	“I’m working with a dolly every day. I’ve got Steadicam for a couple of weeks,” he says. “I’m like a kid in a candy store. I’m ready to move around and make it pop. The language of the Japanese filmmakers I love is very dynamic. When I think about Imamura or Ōshima or Miki or Obayashi, they’re constantly experimenting with different techniques within the same picture. I definitely wanted to capture that spirit as well. So it was really fun for me. And I think when you have fun filmmaking, I know it comes across on screen.”

	Kotlyarenko’s insistence on tech-based verisimilitude included elements on set that would otherwise just be added later in post.

	“Before we ever went to Japan, before our production really started principal, we had to shoot Carter in the cave because I needed to have an edit of that and the livestream,” he says. “I need to write the livestream so that Izumi, when she shows her boyfriend what she’s watching, it’s there. I don’t want to have a green screen on a phone. I want that to be ready so that the timing of what they’re interacting with on their phones is real.”

	Ultimately, despite its modern feel, Kotlyarenko says “Vintage Violence” speaks to a core idea of cinema.

	“If you’ve ever had an opportunity in a public space to just errantly see someone else’s phone, maybe by accident, maybe you’re peeking, that’s a really thrilling form of voyeurism,” he says. “The history of cinema is, in a way, the history of voyeurism. With phones, you have this awesome opportunity to engage in a type of voyeurism that has barely been explored in cinema, but it’s so real. That’s an exciting prospect for me.”

schema.headline: Is ‘Vintage Violence’ the Future of Movies? Inside the Frantic Chase Movie Built for Phone-Addicted Audiences: It’s a ‘New Approach to Viewing’

	Sherri Shepherd is stepping back into the spotlight this weekend with a new film that tells the true story of a 9/11 survivor.

	The actress stars in “Angel in the Rubble: The Genelle Guzman Story,” which premieres on Lifetime this Saturday, Sept. 12 at 8 p.m. Executive produced by Shepherd, along with Robin Roberts, Linda Berman and Anne Carlucci, the film recounts the survival story of Genelle Guzman (Shepherd), a New York City transit worker who was buried beneath the North Tower after it collapsed on Sept. 11, 2001.
	

	Guzman was trapped for 27 hours before rescuers found her clinging to life under the rubble. According to a movie description, the then-30-year-old was the final survivor recovered from Ground Zero.


	Viewers can watch “Angel in the Rubble: The Genelle Guzman Story” live on Lifetime this Saturday night, with the network rebroadcasting the made-for-TV movie throughout the weekend. 

	Don’t have cable? Viewers can stream the film as it airs on TV through a live streaming service like Sling. The popular streamer carries a live Lifetime feed on its Sling Blue or Sling Orange packages, both of which start at just $45.99/month. A subscription includes access to 30+ live television channels that you can stream online, plus the ability to stream on up to three devices at a time (for Sling Blue customers).

	Don’t want to commit to a monthly plan? Sling Orange offers a 1-Day Pass that gets you unlimited streaming to all the channels on the platform for just $4.99 for 24 hours. Use the pass to watch “Angel in the Rubble” online without cable as it airs on TV. There is no commitment to continue on with a monthly plan after your Day Pass expires.
	

	You can also watch the film on-demand the next day online at mylifetime.com, the network’s official streaming site.

	This is one of Shepherd’s first major roles since the TV host and comedian’s eponymous talk show ended this summer. The film, meantime, is based on Guzman (now married and known as Guzman-McMillan’s) 2011 memoir of the same name.

	Per a Lifetime description, “The film recounts the extraordinary survival of Genelle Guzman. As she fought to stay alive, Genelle reflected on her life and the faith she had left behind, praying for deliverance and promising to change if given another chance.  Her prayers were answered when a man named Paul found her in the debris and remained by her side until rescuers pulled her to safety—the final survivor recovered from Ground Zero. When Genelle later searched for Paul to thank him, no one could confirm he was ever there, leading her to believe he was an angel sent to save her and guide her toward the renewed life she had promised while buried beneath the rubble.”

title: Marvel’s ‘X-Men’ Reboot Casts ‘Gen V’ Star Asa Germann as Angel
description:
Marvel’s “X-Men” cast is expanding with the addition of “Gen V” star Asa Germann as the high-flying mutant Angel, Variety can confirm.

	He joins th
body:
Marvel’s “X-Men” cast is expanding with the addition of “Gen V” star Asa Germann as the high-flying mutant Angel, Variety can confirm.

	He joins the new mutant team consisting of Sadie Sink as Jean Grey, Kit Connor as Cyclops, Samara Weaving as Emma Frost, Inde Navarrette as Rogue, Christopher Abbott as Prof. X and Maya Boyd as Storm. Marvel Studios chief Kevin Feige revealed the new “X-Men” cast at last month’s D23 convention. 


	Adam Driver will be playing the classic “X-Men” comic-book villain Mr. Sinister in the film, helmed by “Thunderbolts” director Jake Schreier. The movie will release on May 5, 2028. 
	

	Angel’s real name is Warren Worthington III, and he can fly thanks to his large, bird-like wings. He previously appeared in Fox’s “X-Men: The Last Stand,” played as a kid in a flashback by Ben Foster and as an adult by Cayden Boyd. Ben Hardy starred as the character in “X-Men: Apocalypse” as his evil alter-ego Archangel, who has metallic wings.

	Germann first broke out in Amazon Prime Video’s superhero satire “Gen V,” a spinoff of “The Boys.” He played Sam Riordan, a schizophrenic hero who is near invulnerable and has massive strength. He attends classes at Godolkin University, a school for young supes, but becomes brain-washed and flips sides to fight against his former friends in Season 2 before they rescue him. Germann also appeared in two episodes of “The Boys” Season 4; “Gen V” was canceled earlier this year after two seasons. He also played Lucas Bowden in this year’s “Scream 7” and appeared in an episode of Netflix’s “Dahmer – Monster: The Jeffrey Dahmer Story.”
	

	Marvel did not comment on the casting. Hollywood Reporter first reported the news.

schema.headline: Marvel’s ‘X-Men’ Reboot Casts ‘Gen V’ Star Asa Germann as Angel

title: Paul Walker’s Brother Says AI Could Bring Actor Back for Final ‘Fast and Furious’ Movie but ‘I Would Not Be Interested in Doing That’
description: Paul Walker‘s brother does not want to be involved in bringing back the late actor’s character, Brian O’Conner, for Universal’s next “Fast and Furio
body:
Paul Walker‘s brother does not want to be involved in bringing back the late actor’s character, Brian O’Conner, for Universal’s next “Fast and Furious” movie. He knows AI could be used to do it, but he doesn’t think it should be done. 

	“AI was not a thing back in 2014, so they could do that,” Cody Walker told Entertainment Weekly. “There’s years of footage that was never used from these other ‘Fast’ films. They’re the best in the business, they can figure that out.”
	

	Even if the “Fast and Furious” team doesn’t use AI, Cody Walker is “not interested” in stepping in as a stunt double for 2028’s “Fast Forever.” The decision to bring him back for the finale, he said, should ultimately come down to Paul’s daughter, Meadow.


	“My stance is, it’s what Meadow wants to see done; it’s her father,” Walker said. “I would not be interested in doing that again. I love the way his character exited the franchise. They didn’t kill him off, they didn’t do something cheesy like that. It’s beautiful, [Brian] is off raising his kids. But if they want to do that, if Meadow would like to see that, they don’t need me or Caleb.”

	Cody and Caleb Walker previously stood in for Paul after he died in a car crash on a break from filming “Furious 7” in 2013. With the help of visual effects, “Furious 7” was completed and gave Paul’s character a graceful exit. Back in 2018, his brothers were not against returning to the franchise in the future. 

	“I just hope we get to have a little cameo and bring Paul back to save the day and I get to help create that again,” Caleb had told Entertainment Weekly at the time, with Cody adding, “I think there could potentially be a way to do it. But it would take a lot of thought and it’d have to be tasteful.”
	

	Cody’s current stance against a cameo comes in opposition to “Fast” star Vin Diesel’s insistence on bringing Paul’s character Brian back for the finale.

	“The studio said to me, ‘Vin, can we please have the finale of Fast & Furious [in] April 2027?’” Diesel told Vanity Fair in 2025. “I said, ‘Under three conditions.’ The first is to bring the franchise back to L.A. The second thing was to return to the car culture, to the street racing. The third thing was reuniting Dom and Brian O’Conner. That is what you’re going to get in the finale.” 

	The supposedly final installment of the decades-long franchise “Fast Forever” hits theaters March 17, 2028. It’s still unclear, even to Cody, whether or not it will have one last scene of Paul. 

	“I have no idea what to expect there,” Cody said. “I talked to Vin, and when it comes to this whole process, he gets very ethereal; it’s a lot of weight. The guy is incredible, he’s extremely gifted, he takes this very seriously and there’s a mountain on Vin’s shoulders. He wants this to be the best one and as good as it can be because it’s the final [one].”

schema.headline: Paul Walker’s Brother Says AI Could Bring Actor Back for Final ‘Fast and Furious’ Movie but ‘I Would Not Be Interested in Doing That’

title: ‘Hawaii Five-O’ Movie in the Works From ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Director Destin Daniel Cretton
description:
A movie version of the police procedural “Hawaii Five-O” is in the works at Paramount. 

	Destin Daniel Cretton, whose summer blockbuster “Spider-Ma
body:
A movie version of the police procedural “Hawaii Five-O” is in the works at Paramount. 

	Destin Daniel Cretton, whose summer blockbuster “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” has remained a box office sensation, has been hired to direct the film from a script by Chris Bremner (“Bad Boys for Life”).

	Plot details haven’t been revealed as the project is in early stages of development, according to sources. Deadline Hollywood broke the news of the reboot.
	

	Created by Leonard Freeman, “Hawaii Five-O” launched in 1968 and became the longest-running police drama on American television by the finale in 1980. The series starred Jack Lord as detective captain Steve McGarrett, who investigated organized crime as the head of a fictional elite state police task force on the island. Most episodes ended with the show’s catchphrase “Book ’em, Dano” — which McGarrett would say to his partner, detective Danny Williams (played by James MacArthur) after a suspect was caught.


	A reboot called “Hawaii Five-0” (using a zero instead of the original letter “O”) launched on CBS in 2010 and ran for 10 seasons, with the final 240th episode airing in 2020. Alex O’Loughlin, Scott Caan, Daniel Dae Kim and Grace Park anchored the new series, which put a modern spin on the cop drama. There have been several attempts over the decades to bring a “Hawaii Five-O” movie to the big screen but none came to fruition.

	Cretton is best known for his work on Marvel’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings.” The latest Spidey adventure, which opened in late July, has grossed a stunning $924 million domestically and $2.4 billion globally to date. It’s on the verge of becoming the highest-grossing North American release in history (supplanting 2015’s “Star Wars: The Force Awakens” with $936 million, not adjusted for inflation) and it’s the third-biggest movie worldwide following 2009’s “Avatar” ($2.9 billion) and 2019’s “Avengers: Endgame” ($2.79 billion).

schema.headline: ‘Hawaii Five-O’ Movie in the Works From ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Director Destin Daniel Cretton

title: Nicholas Sparks’ ‘Counting Miracles’ Adaptation at Amazon to Be Helmed by ‘The Peanut Butter Falcon’ Filmmaker Tyler Nilson (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Amazon MGM Studios’ adaptation of the Nicholas Sparks bestseller “Counting Miracles” has found its writer/director in “The Peanut Butter Falcon” co-
body:
Amazon MGM Studios’ adaptation of the Nicholas Sparks bestseller “Counting Miracles” has found its writer/director in “The Peanut Butter Falcon” co-filmmaker Tyler Nilson.

	Starring Alan Ritchson, “Counting Miracles” follows Army Ranger Tanner Hughes (Ritchson) as he crosses the country comforting the families of fallen soldiers until a mysterious letter sends him searching for the father he never knew. His journey leads him to a small town, where a blossoming romance with a doctor and single mother of two draws him into the life of a reclusive old man with a haunting past. As their lives become unexpectedly intertwined, Tanner is forced to confront the truth of who he is — and discover where he truly belongs.
	

	In collaboration with Nilson and Sparks, “Counting Miracles” will be produced by Ritchson via his Dancing Skeleton banner alongside Di Novi Pictures’ Denise Di Novi and Margaret French Isaac and Sparks’s longtime producing partner Theresa Park. Currently, Dancing Skeleton and Di Novi Pictures are under first-look film deals with Amazon MGM Studios and Ritchson has a three-picture acting deal with the company.


	Nilson’s breakout came with 2019’s “The Peanut Butter Falcon,” which he co-wrote and co-directed with Michael Schwartz as their feature debut. Starring Shia LaBeouf, Dakota Johnson and Zack Gottsagen, the film won the Audience Award at SXSW, earned a DGA nomination for Achievement in First-Time Feature Film, landed on the NBR’s Top Ten Independent Films list and became the highest-grossing indie release of the year.
	

	Next up for Nilson was 2024’s “Los Frikis,” which he co-wrote and directed with Schwartz and was produced by Phil Lord and Christopher Miller. Starring Adria Arjona and Héctor Medina, the film was set in 1990s Cuba.

	Best known for his novels including “The Notebook,” “A Walk to Remember,” “Message in a Bottle,” “Dear John,” “The Last Song,” “Safe Haven,” “The Longest Ride” and “The Choice,” Sparks is no stranger to a Hollywood adaptation. His novels have been made into films that have collectively grossed more than $750 million worldwide, with Sparks serving as a producer on several adaptations. 

	Aside from “Counting Miracles,” Sparks’ next big film adaptation is “Remain,” which stars Jake Gyllenhaal and is set to release Feb. 5, 2027. 

	He is repped by Howie Sanders, co-head of the Anonymous Content media rights department, Celeste Fine of Park & Fine Literary and Media, Jill Fritzo PR and Scott Schwimer Esq.

schema.headline: Nicholas Sparks’ ‘Counting Miracles’ Adaptation at Amazon to Be Helmed by ‘The Peanut Butter Falcon’ Filmmaker Tyler Nilson (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Andrew Scott to Receive Mill Valley Film Festival’s Acting Award for ‘Elsinore’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Andrew Scott will receive the Mill Valley Film Festival‘s Acting Award for his latest performance in “Elsinore.”

	Scott stars in the Focus Features
body:
Andrew Scott will receive the Mill Valley Film Festival‘s Acting Award for his latest performance in “Elsinore.”

	Scott stars in the Focus Features film portraying Ian Charleson in his celebrated performance as Hamlet at London’s National Theatre, before the actor, known for starring in “Chariots of Fire,” died at the peak of the AIDS crisis in 1990.

	Directed by Simon Stone and produced by Scott, “Elsinore” tells the deeply emotional and inspirational true story of the late Charleson, a gifted actor whose greatest challenge becomes his greatest triumph. “Facing his own mortality with unflinching honesty, wit, and grace,” the film’s synopsis explains, “Charleson delivers a courageous performance that becomes a source of healing and inspiration for those around him.” Focus will release “Elsinore,” also starring Oscar winner Olivia Colman, in theaters on Nov. 20.
	

	MVFF49 takes place Oct. 1-11 across venues in Marin County and the Bay Area. The California Film Institute, a nonprofit that also runs the DocLands Documentary Film Festival, presents the festival. Scott’s Actor Award presentation will take place on Saturday, Oct. 3, at 7 p.m. at the Smith Rafael Film Center as part of MVFF49’s Spotlight program, which recognizes standout work by film artists at any stage in their career.


	“Devastating and miraculous, Andrew Scott gives the performance of a lifetime as an actor racing mortality to claim Hamlet before the curtain falls,” said Mark Fishkin, founder and director of the Mill Valley Film Festival, in a statement. “Olivia Colman quietly breaks your heart as the only one who knows the truth. Urgent, unforgettable, and deeply moving.”
	

	The festival’s artistic director Rose Kuo added: “Andrew Scott’s interpretation of Ian Charleson’s Hamlet, the most death-haunted of tragic heroes, is witty, superbly passionate, and profoundly moving, becoming a meditation on mortality and the art of acting itself.”

	Variety chief awards editor Clayton Davis declared that playing Charleson in “Elsinore” is “the role of Scott’s career” and could land him his first best actor Oscar nomination, recognition that has eluded the actor thus far, including a notable snub for his shattering turn in “All of Us Strangers.”  

	The Mill Valley award is the latest accolade for Scott, who previously won SAG-AFTRA’s Actor Award for his role in “Fleabag” and three Olivier Awards for “Vanya,” “A Girl in a Car with a Man” and “Present Laughter.” In 2024, he earned Emmy, Golden Globe and Critics’ Choice nominations for starring in Netflix’s “Ripley.” He also became the first person to win Critics Circle lead actor prizes in both film and theater in the same year for “All of Us Strangers” and “Vanya.”

	Scott most recently starred in Focus’s “Pressure,” opposite Oscar winner Brendan Fraser, as well as the third installment of the “Knives Out” franchise, “Wake Up Dead Man” and Richard Linklater’s “Blue Moon,” which earned Scott the Berlin Film Festival’s Silver Bear award (for best supporting performance), ahead of the film’s Academy Award and Golden Globe nominations. Next year, he stars in “A Place in Hell” for Neon, alongside Michelle Williams and Daisy Edgar-Jones. He recently wrapped production on Netflix’s “Walk the Blue Fields” opposite Emily Blunt, and Justine Triet’s next film, “Fonda,” alongside Mia Goth.

schema.headline: Andrew Scott to Receive Mill Valley Film Festival’s Acting Award for ‘Elsinore’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: France Unveils Shortlist of Five Films for the International Oscar Race, From ‘Minotaur’ to ‘De Gaulle’ and ‘Iron Boy’
description: France has unveiled a robust shortlist of five films in the pipeline to represent country in the best international feature film race at Oscars, wit
body:
France has unveiled a robust shortlist of five films in the pipeline to represent country in the best international feature film race at Oscars, with Andrey Zvyagintsev’s Cannes Grand Prize winner “Minotaur” and Antonin Baudry’s WW2-set “The Battle of De Gaulle: The Iron Age” among the titles that made the cut. 

	Unveiled Thursday by France’s National Film Board, the eclectic shortlist also includes Arthur Harari’s “The Unknown” starring Lea Seydoux and and Niels Schneider, Louis Clichy’s animated feature “Iron Boy” and Marine Atlan’s “La Gradiva.”
	

	“Minotaur,” a scathing portrait of corruption in Putin’s Russia, is directed by Zvyagintsev, the acclaimed Russian filmmaker behind “Leviathan” who lives in France with asylum status and used his acceptance speech to urge Putin to end the war. Mubi has U.S. distribution on the film.


	While “Minotaur” has the largest prestige pedigree and momentum, it’s facing a wide range of rivals in the race. “De Gaulle” hails from Pathé Films and forms part of the filmmaker’s epic saga about Charles de Gaulle’s emergence as a leader of the French Resistance. The first opus bowed out of competition at Cannes where it earned stellar reviews. The two movies have so far drawn more than five million admissions in France. A U.S. distribution deal will be announced in the coming days. 

	Harari’s “The Unknown,” meanwhile, marks the filmmaker’s return behind the camera following “Onoda: 10,000 Nights in the Jungle.” The body-swapping drama competed at Cannes and is handled by Neon. Harari is also rolling off Justine Triet’s Palme d’Or-winning “Anatomy of a Fall,” for which the pair won the Oscar for original screenplay. 
	

	“La Gradiva” also comes to the race with Cannes momentum after winning the Grand Prize at Critics’ Week. The coming-of-age melodrama follows a French class trip to Pompeii and is represented internationally by MK2 Films. It’s been acquired by 1-2 Special.

	Rounding out the shortlist is Louis Clichy’s hand-painted animated feature “Iron Boy,” which was acquired by Sony Pictures Classics after premiering at Cannes’ Un Certain Regard where it won the Special Jury Prize, and went on to win three awards at Annecy. Clichy, an animation filmmaker whose credits include the “Asterix” franchise, gives France a solid animated contender that follow the footsteps of “Flow” which won best animated film in 2025 and was also nominated in the international feature category (where it represented Latvia). 

	France’s Oscar selection committee, whose makeup is now kept confidential, will reconvene on Sept. 16 to hear presentations from the producers and international sales agents behind each shortlisted film, as well as their U.S. distributors. The debate is expected to be particularly vibrant considering that some members on the committee are said to be reluctant to select a foreign director whose film is not in French. Last year’s decision to pick Iran’s Jafar Panahi, and his Palme d’Or winner “It Was Just an Accident” over Richard Linklater’s French-language “Nouvelle Vague,” had sparked some backlash. The movie was ultimately nominated for best international feature and original screenplay. 

	France has one of the strongest historical records in the international feature category but has not won the Oscar since Régis Wargnier’s “Indochine” took the prize in 1993.

schema.headline: France Unveils Shortlist of Five Films for the International Oscar Race, From ‘Minotaur’ to ‘De Gaulle’ and ‘Iron Boy’

title: ‘Oh, Mary!’ Set for HBO With Cole Escola Reprising Lead Role in Filmed Stage Play
description:
A filmed version of the hit Broadway and West End play “Oh, Mary!” will debut on HBO in 2027.

	HBO dropped the news in a teaser featuring playwrigh
body:
A filmed version of the hit Broadway and West End play “Oh, Mary!” will debut on HBO in 2027.

	HBO dropped the news in a teaser featuring playwright and star Cole Escola opposite “Sex and the City” stars Sarah Jessica Parker and Cynthia Nixon. As Mary Todd Lincoln, Escola rushes into the HBO offices and says, “Hello. I would like to do my play here, please.” An unseen receptionist gives Escola directions, but as they begin to run down the hall, the receptionist stops them. The “Sex and the City” theme music begins to play as she asks, “Oh, wait! Would you like some water?” and the camera reveals that Escola has been talking to Parker. Then Nixon appears, carrying a glass of water on a silver platter. “No, I wouldn’t,” Escola says, scampering away. “That’ll be nice to have around,” Parker muses.
	

	The HBO special was filmed during the July 28, 2026 performance of “Oh, Mary!” in London. Escola stars as Mary alongside Giles Terera as Mary’s Husband (aka Abraham Lincoln), Bianca Leigh as Mary’s Chaperone, Tony Macht as Mary’s Husband’s Assistant and Michael Urie as Mary’s Teacher. 


	Per the official logline, the dark comedy follows “a miserable, suffocated Mary Todd Lincoln in the weeks leading up to Abraham Lincoln’s assassination. Unrequited yearning, alcoholism and suppressed desires abound in this 80-minute, one-act play that finally examines the forgotten life and dreams of Mrs. Lincoln, through the lens of an idiot (playwright Cole Escola).”

	Sam Pinkleton was the play’s original Broadway director and also directed the special. Executive producers include Escola; Alex Bach and Daniel Powell for Irony Point; Carlee Briglia and Mike Lavoie for Mike & Carlee Productions; and Kevin McCollum and Lucas McMahon for Alchemation.
	

	“I’m so happy to share this show with a wider audience and spread ‘Oh, Mary!’ awareness,” Escola said in a statement. “Knowing about ‘Oh, Mary!’ is the first step in getting rid of it.”

	“I fell in love with theater as a kid by absolutely wearing out the VHS tapes of ‘Cats’ and ‘Into The Woods’ and I am honored to continue that legacy with ‘Oh, Mary!’ on HBO,” said Pinkleton. “Shepherding ‘Oh, Mary!’ through its many lives (and Marys) has been an ecstatic experience and I’m giddy that the genius of original idiot Cole Escola will now be immortalized on televisions across America and beyond.”

	See the teaser below.

schema.headline: ‘Oh, Mary!’ Set for HBO With Cole Escola Reprising Lead Role in Filmed Stage Play

title: 'Cat in the Hat' Creeper Allegedly Followed Teenage Girl
description:
'Cat in the Hat' Creeper
                          Allegedly Chased After Teenage Girl
body:
'Cat in the Hat' Creeper
                          Allegedly Chased After Teenage Girl
                          ... Viral Trend Crosses Line
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 10, 2026
                            8:55 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            "The Cat in the Hat" brings a lot of fun to children in Dr. Seuss' original book ... but apparently it's not so fun in real life when the cat starts chasing after you.
      
    
            According to the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, a teenage girl was walking down a residential street in British Columbia around 9 PM on August 24 when a person dressed as the famous feline allegedly followed her down the block.
      
    
            Cops say they have the suspect on video ... and they released an image of them dressed in the full Cat in the Hat 'fit ... including the iconic striped hat, the gloves, and the cat bodysuit.
      

      
        
              
    
    
            Thankfully, the young lady made it home safely ... though Cpl. Devon Gerrits of the West Kelowna Royal Canadian Mounted Police made it clear this behavior is never funny -- regardless of whether it's supposed to be a joke.
      
    
            Cops are asking anyone who may have doorbell footage in the area to contact them while they investigate.
      
    
            Apparently, this Cat in the Hat character is far from the only person using the fun character for mischief. A.I.-generated clips of the cat are making the rounds online ... and, in them, threats are allegedly being made against specific schools and communities.
      
    
            At least 10 juveniles have reportedly been arrested in connection with the not-so-funny trend.
      
    
            A new "Cat in the Hat" flick is set to come out in November ... and, hopefully, he's not stalking teens in the movie!

body:
Secret Service Agent
                          Caught With Pants Down During Masturbation Bust
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 10, 2026
                            9:45 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            A Secret Service agent's masturbation bust is as embarrassing as you'd expect ... body cam video caught him in a hotel hallway with his belt undone.
      
    
            TMZ obtained the arrest footage from the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office ... you can see the tasers trained on John Spillman as authorities yell at him to get up against the wall.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As he starts to slide down the wall, you can see his belt's unbuckled and his pants are undone before authorities pin him to the ground and cuff him.
      

            That's when someone comes out of the hotel room to talk to the deputies before they take him away.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Spillman admits to having "too much to drink" and asks the officers if he can pull his pants up ... but no dice.
      
    
            As we previously reported, he was arrested for indecent exposure back in May at the DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Miami Airport & Convention Center ... after he allegedly followed hotel guests from the hotel lobby to their room and started rubbing one out in the hallway.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Spillman was reportedly in Florida working perimeter security as part of President Trump's visit to Trump National Doral Golf Club for the 2026 PGA Cadillac Championship ... and was said to be off duty when he was busted.
      
    
            This may not be the last video we see from this bust ... prosecutors are hunting for video of him in the act.
      
    
            Stay tuned ...
